purpose: Accuracy, stability and single-thread speed of RapidGLM against the standard R and Python GLM fitters, and its drop-in interfaces.
reference: Damped Newton in IEEE binary128 (benchmarks/glm/reference.cpp); NB theta by profile bisection over [1e-6, 1e8].
accuracy_scope: Problems with a finite, identifiable MLE, excluding relative collinearity 1e-12 (aliased by R's threshold). Failure: error, missing identifiable coefficient, or coefficient error above 1e-3 reference standard errors.

speed_scope: Minimum over up to seven repeats (15 s budget) of a fit on loaded in-memory data, one physical core, one BLAS/OpenMP thread. Every tool/problem command starts after the retained quiet predicate. Tool defaults unless marked tight; waits are excluded.

environment.note: One AMD Threadripper PRO 5965WX workstation (Zen 3). Timed work uses one thread per physical core on CPUs 6-21, with SMT siblings 30-45 idle; one thread uses CPU 6, eight use 6-13, twelve use 6-17. Drivers and untimed checks use CPUs 0-5. Exclusive Slurm allocation; schedutil governor, boost enabled and SMT enabled, unchanged. Each timed command starts after two ten-second quiet samples. More than 5% other CPU activity on selected cores or any sibling invalidates the command. Host load, other-user processes and vLLM CPU use are retained per command. From the resumed bulk stage on 2026-11-03, a user-authorized runtime service cpuset confines vLLM to CPUs 0-5,22-29,46-47; the reservation receipt records its application and restoration. Earlier accepted measurements retain their original guarded host conditions.
